review_snapshot.stem: Which statement best describes lead-acid battery charging behavior?

choices.A: Charging behavior depends on state of charge and the charger or regulator strategy.
choices.B: Charging behavior is the same at every state of charge if battery voltage is above a fixed threshold.
choices.C: Charging behavior is determined only by battery age and is independent of the charger or regulator strategy.
choices.D: Charging behavior can be evaluated with one universal charging-current value for all lead-acid batteries.

review_snapshot.explanation: Lead-acid battery charging behavior varies with state of charge and the charging or regulation strategy. Chemistry-specific and manufacturer-specific procedures still control any diagnostic limits or service decisions.
review_snapshot.source_final_content_text: Lead-acid battery charging behavior depends on state of charge and the charger or regulator strategy.

review_snapshot.stem: During constant-voltage charging of a discharged lead-acid battery, which current trend is most consistent with the approved instructional concept?

choices.A: Charging current must remain constant until the battery reaches full charge.
choices.B: Charging current may be high initially and then decrease as battery voltage rises toward full charge.
choices.C: Charging current must increase continuously as battery voltage rises.
choices.D: A single fixed amperage value determines whether every lead-acid battery is charging correctly.

review_snapshot.explanation: Under constant-voltage charging, a discharged lead-acid battery may initially accept high current, and current decreases as battery voltage rises toward full charge. The concept describes a trend, not a universal automotive amperage pass/fail value.
review_snapshot.source_final_content_text: Under constant-voltage charging, a discharged lead-acid battery may initially accept high current, and charging current decreases as battery voltage rises toward full charge.

review_snapshot.stem: Why can increased electrical charging demand increase mechanical load on an engine with a belt-driven charging system?

choices.A: The charging system converts additional mechanical input into electrical output, so greater electrical demand can require more mechanical power from the engine.
choices.B: Electrical demand eliminates mechanical resistance in belt-driven accessories, reducing the power required from the engine.
choices.C: Charging demand changes only battery voltage and has no relationship to mechanical power transfer.
choices.D: Any increase in charging demand proves a specific fuel-consumption increase regardless of vehicle design or operating condition.

review_snapshot.explanation: Electrical charging demand and belt-driven auxiliaries require mechanical power from the engine. The approved concept supports the direction of the load relationship, but it does not establish a universal fuel-consumption value, charging-output threshold, or diagnostic limit.
review_snapshot.source_final_content_text: Electrical charging demand and belt-driven auxiliaries increase mechanical load on the engine.
